Agents – Purview controls quick guide

Catalog read: October 28, 2026 at 10:27 PM | PH weekly automation

What to turn on, who can do it, where to click, what to expect, and what still needs proof. Public guidance checked 8 Oct 2026; no live agent validation claimed.

Same numbered control-card format as the CP/CW guide. Videos: public-guidance reconstructions, not live recordings.

Scripts unavailable: the full eleven-card guide is readable below. Video captions/transcripts and procedures remain available as static content.

How to use this

  • Pick a numbered control card. Each has roles, click paths, wait times, result checks, licensing, gotchas and a video walkthrough.
  • Keep Agent Builder/declarative, Studio/custom-engine and ordinary Copilot separate; record the exact channel, identity, source and tools.
  • These are public-guidance illustrations, not live tenant recordings or test results.
  • Use the protected Word validation draft for real evidence. Its content is not embedded here.
Agent types — do not substitute one test for another
TypeBoundary
Agent Builder / declarativeCopilot-hosted grounding/actions. Verify the actual agent attribution and supported capture/policy path.
Studio / custom-enginePublished channel, environment, authentication, sources and tools determine coverage.
Ordinary Microsoft 365 CopilotBaseline only; not evidence of an agent test.

How long to wait

ControlWhat to expect / when
eDiscovery / AuditAsynchronous capture/indexing. Record exact UTC window and actual recheck time.
DLP / labelsAllow policy publication/distribution and source processing; inspect actual policy-linked outcome.
CC / IRMAsynchronous review/scoring. Role assignments can take up to 30 minutes.
RetentionExchange processing 1–7 days, later deletion runs and holds; discoverability is not a duration guarantee.
Restricted discoveryVariable site propagation; no permission change and no universal agent denial.

School licensing — verify the actual feature

School licensing questionCheck before deployment
A3 / base controlsFeature-level Audit, eDiscovery, manual labels and retention entitlements vary. Do not assume base licensing includes every advanced AI control.
A5 / compliance add-onsCheck Premium eDiscovery, Audit retention, Communication Compliance, Insider Risk and advanced DLP/labels individually.
Studio / Power PlatformVerify published channel, source, connector and environment prerequisites. PAYG AI data/billing can apply; Copilot licensing alone is not universal telemetry.
SharePoint discoveryCheck current Copilot/SharePoint Advanced Management eligibility; RCD is a SharePoint site feature, not a OneDrive control.
Microsoft Purview service description
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description
Evidence-confidence matrix — what each state actually proves
Confidence stateRequired evidenceDoes not prove
ConfiguredPolicy exists, mode/scope/roles documented.Capture, enforcement or coverage of every agent/tool.
CapturedActual supported interaction/metadata matched to the run.Blocking, retention duration or cross-tool correlation from counts.
EnforcedPolicy-attributable restriction on an identified supported path; allowed control succeeds.Universal coverage for other sources, identities, channels or MCP tools.
UnconfirmedMissing/ambiguous evidence, unsupported path or unresolved confounder.Do not promote to a pass because a screen, inventory or score exists.

Every scene in this guide is illustrative. No tenant validation state is asserted.

Card 1 Supported path · validation unconfirmed

eDiscovery: find what a user asked an agent

Video transcript

Title. Let's walk through card 1. eDiscovery: find what a user asked an agent. Can we find an agent's prompt and response in an investigation? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged starting point: the eDiscovery Manager subgroup, with access to the case and the search/export permissions needed for the task. The eDiscovery Administrator subgroup also works and can access all cases. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Purview → eDiscovery → Cases. Use an authorized case, then create a search; do not run deletion workflows.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Under data sources, add the approved test user's Exchange Online mailbox. Source-file discovery is a separate SharePoint/OneDrive search.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Use the Copilot activity condition, a harmless synthetic marker and a UTC date interval enclosing the entire run.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. For Studio, Microsoft lists IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.Copilot.Studio.*. Confirm the actual returned item class rather than assuming all agents use that class.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. Run the search, then review statistics and available sample/review results. Open the specific content item, not just the total count.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. Correlate content, time and available Audit agent/host metadata. Keep original content and identifiers only in the protected case or Word validation record.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Search statistics and the actual content item in the intended mailbox. Audit correlation for agent identity, host and run time; source file and tool checks remain separate. Allow capture and indexing before searching. Record the actual UTC search window and recheck time; no fixed agent indexing SLA is claimed here. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Add the intended mailbox. Use a UTC interval that encloses the run. Read actual content, not just counts. Correlate the agent and channel. Keep real evidence protected. An exclusive end time before a conversation cannot include it. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Can we find an agent's prompt and response in an investigation?For supported captured interactions, search the user's Exchange mailbox. Confirm the agent and channel; a mailbox search total alone does not identify one agent or correlate several tools.

Who can do this

Least-privileged starting point: the eDiscovery Manager subgroup, with access to the case and the search/export permissions needed for the task. The eDiscovery Administrator subgroup also works and can access all cases. Do not grant Search And Purge for a search-only validation. Content viewing and export must be authorized separately.

How to set it up

  1. Open Purview → eDiscovery → Cases. Use an authorized case, then create a search; do not run deletion workflows.
  2. Under data sources, add the approved test user's Exchange Online mailbox. Source-file discovery is a separate SharePoint/OneDrive search.
  3. Use the Copilot activity condition, a harmless synthetic marker and a UTC date interval enclosing the entire run.
  4. For Studio, Microsoft lists IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.Copilot.Studio.*. Confirm the actual returned item class rather than assuming all agents use that class.
  5. Run the search, then review statistics and available sample/review results. Open the specific content item, not just the total count.
  6. Correlate content, time and available Audit agent/host metadata. Keep original content and identifiers only in the protected case or Word validation record.

How long to wait

Allow capture and indexing before searching. Record the actual UTC search window and recheck time; no fixed agent indexing SLA is claimed here.

Where to check the result

  • Search statistics and the actual content item in the intended mailbox.
  • Audit correlation for agent identity, host and run time; source file and tool checks remain separate.

Licensing for schools

  • Use the Purview service description's eDiscovery feature table for your A3/A5 or add-on entitlement; basic search and Premium review/analytics are different features.
  • Check the agent experience, user licensing and capture prerequisites. The Studio logging documentation has Microsoft 365 licensing/channel prerequisites.

  • Studio capture prerequisites

Watch out for

  • An exclusive end time before a conversation cannot include it.
  • Several records or matching counts do not prove one conversation across several tools.
  • A normal Copilot record is not automatically a declarative or Studio agent record.

Audit: which agent, where, and what it accessed

Video transcript

Title. Let's walk through card 2. Audit: which agent, where, and what it accessed. Can we tell which agent handled a request and which resources it used? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged search role: Audit Reader. Audit Manager also works and has broader audit capabilities; broader compliance/organization role groups may include the required audit roles. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Purview → Audit → Search and confirm auditing is enabled for the applicable scope.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Set a UTC date/time interval that contains the controlled run, with a small clock margin; add the approved test identity.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. In activity operation names, search CopilotInteraction. Search Studio authoring events separately when checking publish or authentication changes.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Run the search, then open a candidate event. Inspect available AgentId, AgentName, AgentVersion, AppHost and AppIdentity.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. Inspect AccessedResources, Messages and available policy/status information. Compare the event with the protected agent inventory and run record.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. For content, use an authorized AI activity or eDiscovery view. Studio Audit logs reference transcript threads; they do not contain the full chat transcript.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Audit search → event details → agent/host/resource fields. Separate AI activity content view where supported and authorized. Audit ingestion is asynchronous and channel-dependent. Recheck a bounded interval after processing; do not reuse an ordinary Copilot lab timing as an agent SLA. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Search CopilotInteraction + identity + UTC. Identify the actual agent, not only its host. Resource metadata is not the full transcript. One action can create several records. No universal tool-coverage claim. The same host can contain ordinary Copilot and agents. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Can we tell which agent handled a request and which resources it used?Audit provides activity metadata on supported paths. Inspect actual AgentId, AgentName, AgentVersion, AppHost and resource fields when present. Missing fields are a gap, not permission to invent them.

Who can do this

Least-privileged search role: Audit Reader. Audit Manager also works and has broader audit capabilities; broader compliance/organization role groups may include the required audit roles. Verify the assigned roles and scope rather than defaulting to Global Administrator. Viewing a related transcript requires separate content permissions.

How to set it up

  1. Open Purview → Audit → Search and confirm auditing is enabled for the applicable scope.
  2. Set a UTC date/time interval that contains the controlled run, with a small clock margin; add the approved test identity.
  3. In activity operation names, search CopilotInteraction. Search Studio authoring events separately when checking publish or authentication changes.
  4. Run the search, then open a candidate event. Inspect available AgentId, AgentName, AgentVersion, AppHost and AppIdentity.
  5. Inspect AccessedResources, Messages and available policy/status information. Compare the event with the protected agent inventory and run record.
  6. For content, use an authorized AI activity or eDiscovery view. Studio Audit logs reference transcript threads; they do not contain the full chat transcript.

How long to wait

Audit ingestion is asynchronous and channel-dependent. Recheck a bounded interval after processing; do not reuse an ordinary Copilot lab timing as an agent SLA.

Where to check the result

  • Audit search → event details → agent/host/resource fields.
  • Separate AI activity content view where supported and authorized.

Licensing for schools

  • Check Audit Standard entitlement in the Purview service description; extended audit retention/Premium features have separate requirements.
  • Studio logging requires applicable Microsoft 365 licensing and supported channels; its documentation notes FedRAMP limitations.

Learn more (Microsoft)

  • Copilot audit schema and fields
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-copilot
  • Studio audit events and exclusions
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-logging-copilot-studio

DLP: prove a supported sensitive-content restriction

Video walkthrough · card 3

189 seconds · Generic reconstruction, not a live tenant capture.

Video transcript

Title. Let's walk through card 3. DLP: prove a supported sensitive-content restriction. Can a policy stop an agent from processing a labelled knowledge file? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged administration can use a scoped custom role group containing DLP Compliance Management. Information Protection Admin/Information Protection, Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator and Security Administrator are documented broader starting points. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Purview → Data Loss Prevention → Policies and inspect an approved test policy; do not broaden production scope for a demonstration.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Check the Microsoft 365 Copilot location, selected users, sensitivity-label condition, action and policy mode.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Confirm the agent's published channel and SharePoint knowledge path are supported. Do not extend this conclusion to arbitrary tools or uploaded files.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Use equivalent synthetic allowed and restricted source cases. Verify effective permissions, encryption rights and retrieval before attributing an answer difference to DLP.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. After policy distribution, run the matched cases and inspect available policy-linked resource/activity evidence for the exact run.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. Record configured, captured, enforced or unconfirmed separately. Only claim restriction when the evidence ties the outcome to the policy and the allowed control works.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Policy scope and enforcement mode. Available DLP activity/resource policy details plus the actual allowed/restricted outcome. Allow policy distribution before testing and activity ingestion before review. No tenant-specific propagation or blocking result is asserted. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Supported source and channel first. Inspect scope, action and policy mode. Keep rights and retrieval equivalent. Seek policy-linked outcome evidence. No DLP claim from refusal alone. Encryption, missing EXTRACT rights, authentication and retrieval can all explain a different answer. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Can a policy stop an agent from processing a labelled knowledge file?Public Studio guidance documents label-based restriction for SharePoint knowledge in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Prove that exact supported path; an unanswered question does not establish DLP causation.

Who can do this

Least-privileged administration can use a scoped custom role group containing DLP Compliance Management. Information Protection Admin/Information Protection, Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator and Security Administrator are documented broader starting points. Scope and reviewer/content access remain separate; use only the permissions needed.

How to set it up

  1. Open Purview → Data Loss Prevention → Policies and inspect an approved test policy; do not broaden production scope for a demonstration.
  2. Check the Microsoft 365 Copilot location, selected users, sensitivity-label condition, action and policy mode.
  3. Confirm the agent's published channel and SharePoint knowledge path are supported. Do not extend this conclusion to arbitrary tools or uploaded files.
  4. Use equivalent synthetic allowed and restricted source cases. Verify effective permissions, encryption rights and retrieval before attributing an answer difference to DLP.
  5. After policy distribution, run the matched cases and inspect available policy-linked resource/activity evidence for the exact run.
  6. Record configured, captured, enforced or unconfirmed separately. Only claim restriction when the evidence ties the outcome to the policy and the allowed control works.

How long to wait

Allow policy distribution before testing and activity ingestion before review. No tenant-specific propagation or blocking result is asserted.

Where to check the result

  • Policy scope and enforcement mode.
  • Available DLP activity/resource policy details plus the actual allowed/restricted outcome.

Licensing for schools

  • Do not infer advanced Copilot DLP entitlement from general A3 DLP. Verify the exact feature under the Purview service description.
  • Check supported knowledge source, agent channel and user prerequisites; configuration availability does not prove runtime support.

Learn more (Microsoft)

  • Purview support for Studio
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-copilot-studio
  • DLP roles and policy deployment
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-deploy-policy

Proposed paired testCompare equivalent synthetic source files on the same supported path.Required: working allowed control and policy-attributable restriction; live outcome unconfirmed.

Watch out for

  • Encryption, missing EXTRACT rights, authentication and retrieval can all explain a different answer.
  • Purview content DLP and Power Platform connector policies are different control planes.
  • A label display or configured rule is not proof of MCP payload inspection.

Communication Compliance: review risky agent prompts

163 seconds · Generic reconstruction, not a live tenant capture.

Video transcript

Title. Let's walk through card 4. Communication Compliance: review risky agent prompts. Can a designated reviewer inspect a supported agent policy match? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged setup group: Communication Compliance Admins. For alert investigation, Communication Compliance Analysts or Investigators plus assignment as a reviewer on the policy. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Purview → Communication Compliance → Policies and create or inspect an approved policy for supported AI interactions.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Select the intended users and Microsoft Copilot experiences source; check the exact agent data and billing prerequisites.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Add authorized reviewers and a harmless synthetic keyword/classification condition. Reviewers should not be the monitored participants.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Run the marked synthetic interaction in the intended published channel, then allow processing.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. Open the policy's Pending tab as an assigned reviewer and inspect the actual match and related prompt/response items.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. Correlate time, application/channel and content to the protected run record. Record whether the prompt, response or both matched.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Communication Compliance → Policies → selected policy → Pending. Reviewer membership, source scope and actual matched content. Policy matching is asynchronous. Role assignments can take up to 30 minutes to apply; record actual processing/recheck times instead of importing CP/CW lab timings. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Supported source and users. Assign authorized reviewers. Use harmless synthetic conditions. Read the actual Pending match. Detection is not prevention. A role without policy reviewer assignment can be insufficient. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Can a designated reviewer inspect a supported agent policy match?Communication Compliance can detect matching prompts/responses for supported AI data. A reviewable match demonstrates detection and review, not real-time prevention.

Who can do this

Least-privileged setup group: Communication Compliance Admins. For alert investigation, Communication Compliance Analysts or Investigators plus assignment as a reviewer on the policy. The broader Communication Compliance group also works. Compliance Administrator/Organization Management can administer the solution but that does not replace reviewer/content authorization.

How to set it up

  1. Open Purview → Communication Compliance → Policies and create or inspect an approved policy for supported AI interactions.
  2. Select the intended users and Microsoft Copilot experiences source; check the exact agent data and billing prerequisites.
  3. Add authorized reviewers and a harmless synthetic keyword/classification condition. Reviewers should not be the monitored participants.
  4. Run the marked synthetic interaction in the intended published channel, then allow processing.
  5. Open the policy's Pending tab as an assigned reviewer and inspect the actual match and related prompt/response items.
  6. Correlate time, application/channel and content to the protected run record. Record whether the prompt, response or both matched.

How long to wait

Policy matching is asynchronous. Role assignments can take up to 30 minutes to apply; record actual processing/recheck times instead of importing CP/CW lab timings.

Where to check the result

  • Communication Compliance → Policies → selected policy → Pending.
  • Reviewer membership, source scope and actual matched content.

Licensing for schools

  • Check Communication Compliance's A5/add-on eligibility in the service description; it is not a universal A3 feature.
  • The AI policy documentation requires pay-as-you-go for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, including Studio. Microsoft 365 Copilot data has different billing treatment.

Learn more (Microsoft)

    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/communication-compliance-copilot
  • Least-privilege roles
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/communication-compliance-permissions

Title. Let's walk through card 5. Insider Risk: distinguish user risk from agent risk. Does a configured or scored agent prove all its tools are monitored? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged policy setup: Insider Risk Management Admins. Alert/case investigation: Insider Risk Management Analysts or Investigators, according to the task. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Purview → Insider Risk Management → Policies. Decide whether the risk object is a user using AI or a supported agent.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Choose the applicable template and inspect prerequisites. Risky Agents guidance lists Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry agents; do not infer declarative coverage from that list.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Inspect actual scope, enabled indicators, triggers and thresholds rather than treating template creation as coverage proof.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Use approved harmless synthetic activity. Do not cause real risky behavior simply to produce an alert.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. As an authorized analyst/investigator, inspect correlated activity, a score or an alert when present. Record exactly which indicator was observed.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. Document untested channels, MCP tools and autonomous paths separately. Keep privacy and reviewer controls intact.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Policy template/prerequisite details. Actual correlated indicator/activity/alert, not only the agent inventory. Signal ingestion, scoring and alerts are asynchronous and depend on prerequisites/thresholds. Role changes can take up to 30 minutes; no guaranteed alert time is claimed. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Choose user risk or agent risk. Check current supported templates. Inspect actual enabled signals. Correlate activity before a claim. Leave untested MCP paths open. A risk score is not a tool-coverage certificate. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Does a configured or scored agent prove all its tools are monitored?No. Risky AI usage and Risky Agents assess different objects. A supported signal or score is an observation; it does not certify MCP, connector or autonomous-run coverage.

Who can do this

Least-privileged policy setup: Insider Risk Management Admins. Alert/case investigation: Insider Risk Management Analysts or Investigators, according to the task. The broader Insider Risk Management group also works. Compliance Administrator/Organization Management can administer the solution; content and forensic permissions remain task-specific.

How to set it up

  1. Open Purview → Insider Risk Management → Policies. Decide whether the risk object is a user using AI or a supported agent.
  2. Choose the applicable template and inspect prerequisites. Risky Agents guidance lists Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry agents; do not infer declarative coverage from that list.
  3. Inspect actual scope, enabled indicators, triggers and thresholds rather than treating template creation as coverage proof.
  4. Use approved harmless synthetic activity. Do not cause real risky behavior simply to produce an alert.
  5. As an authorized analyst/investigator, inspect correlated activity, a score or an alert when present. Record exactly which indicator was observed.
  6. Document untested channels, MCP tools and autonomous paths separately. Keep privacy and reviewer controls intact.

How long to wait

Signal ingestion, scoring and alerts are asynchronous and depend on prerequisites/thresholds. Role changes can take up to 30 minutes; no guaranteed alert time is claimed.

Where to check the result

  • Policy template/prerequisite details.
  • Actual correlated indicator/activity/alert, not only the agent inventory.

Licensing for schools

  • Verify IRM entitlement under A5/add-on or other applicable licensing; scope and signal prerequisites still apply.
  • Check current Risky Agents/Risky AI usage support separately; licensing does not create unsupported telemetry.

Learn more (Microsoft)

  • IRM templates and supported objects
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-policy-templates
  • IRM role groups
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-permissions

Title. Let's walk through card 6. Retention: verify the agent's mailbox protection. Does finding an agent conversation prove it is protected for a year? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged policy administration: a custom role group with Retention Management; for inspection use View-Only Retention Management. The broader Compliance Administrator role group also works. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Purview → Data Lifecycle Management → Retention policies and inspect the approved policy.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. For new policies, check Microsoft Copilot experiences and selected experiences/users. Do not assume a Teams chats policy includes these new locations.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Verify the effective retain/delete action, duration/start basis, policy distribution and intended mailbox inclusion.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Ask the authorized owners to check overlapping retention, litigation/eDiscovery holds and delay holds. Do not remove legal holds for a demo.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. Use eDiscovery to observe the supported synthetic interaction in the intended user's mailbox.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. If duration/deletion validation is required, use an approved disposable lifecycle test and record the actual observations. Visible chat history is not the compliance store.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Effective policy/user/mailbox scope and holds. Supported mailbox content and lifecycle observations; audit-log retention is separate. Exchange processing typically runs within 1–7 days; soft-deleted content remains at least one day before a later eligible deletion run. Holds can suspend deletion. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Inspect effective location and mailbox scope. Check duration, action and holds. Use the compliance store, not chat visibility. Account for backend processing. Discovery alone is not a duration guarantee. A one-day delete setting does not imply deletion tomorrow. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Does finding an agent conversation prove it is protected for a year?No. Present discoverability shows capture now. Verify effective policy location, experience/user scope, mailbox inclusion, duration/action, holds and lifecycle timing before claiming protection for a period.

How to set it up

  6. If duration/deletion validation is required, use an approved disposable lifecycle test and record the actual observations. Visible chat history is not the compliance store.

How long to wait

Exchange processing typically runs within 1–7 days; soft-deleted content remains at least one day before a later eligible deletion run. Holds can suspend deletion.

Title. Let's walk through card 8. Restricted discovery: a site control, not universal agent denial. Does hiding a SharePoint site mean every agent cannot read it? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged default administrator: SharePoint Administrator. A site administrator can manage their own site's setting only when the tenant has explicitly delegated that capability. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open SharePoint admin center → Sites → Active sites and select the approved synthetic test site.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Open Settings → Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot. Inspect the current state; change it only under an approved test change.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Save and allow discovery propagation. Keep source permissions and the test identity constant.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Compare organization-wide discovery with permitted direct access and site-context search; these are different paths.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. For each actual agent, identify whether its knowledge/tool path uses the governed discovery experience or a separate direct/connector path.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. Record results as discovery observations, not universal access denial. Remove the temporary restriction only under the approved change plan.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Site setting/status and organization-wide discovery. Separate direct/site-context/connector behavior for the actual agent. Propagation depends on site size, file count and concurrent updates. Recheck the actual path; no fixed twenty-minute agent result is claimed. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Temporary discovery control. No permission change. SharePoint sites, not OneDrive. Test discovery and direct access separately. Do not substitute a baseline for an agent test. Permissions remain unchanged; direct access may still work. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Does hiding a SharePoint site mean every agent cannot read it?No. Restricted Content Discovery is a temporary site discovery control, not a permission change. It is not supported for OneDrive sites and is not a universal connector/direct-access restriction.

Who can do this

Least-privileged default administrator: SharePoint Administrator. A site administrator can manage their own site's setting only when the tenant has explicitly delegated that capability. Broader tenant roles may also administer SharePoint, but do not grant Global Administrator for this task.

How to set it up

  1. Open SharePoint admin center → Sites → Active sites and select the approved synthetic test site.
  2. Open Settings → Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot. Inspect the current state; change it only under an approved test change.
  3. Save and allow discovery propagation. Keep source permissions and the test identity constant.
  4. Compare organization-wide discovery with permitted direct access and site-context search; these are different paths.
  5. For each actual agent, identify whether its knowledge/tool path uses the governed discovery experience or a separate direct/connector path.
  6. Record results as discovery observations, not universal access denial. Remove the temporary restriction only under the approved change plan.

How long to wait

Propagation depends on site size, file count and concurrent updates. Recheck the actual path; no fixed twenty-minute agent result is claimed.

Where to check the result

  • Site setting/status and organization-wide discovery.
  • Separate direct/site-context/connector behavior for the actual agent.

Licensing for schools

  • RCD is supported for SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites.

Title. Let's walk through card 9. Tools and MCP: govern the exact connector-backed path. Can a Studio data policy stop a tool or MCP connector path? We'll check permissions, follow the click path, then see where to look for evidence. These screens are public-guidance reconstructions, not a live tenant capture.

Who can do this. Start with permissions. Least-privileged starting point: Environment Admin for policies within their permitted environment scope. A Power Platform/tenant administrator can manage broader tenant policy scope. The card lists broader roles and separate content permissions.

Step 1. Now follow the click path. Open Power Platform admin center → Security → Data and privacy → Data policy.

Step 2. Next, check the scope. Inspect the policy's environment scope and the underlying connector's Business, Non-business or Blocked classification.

Step 3. Before continuing, verify this boundary. Identify the exact tool/MCP server and connection identity. Direct custom MCP paths need separate assessment.

Step 4. Here is the controlled test step. Check the applicable connector/action/endpoint restriction. Advanced connector policies govern supported real connectors/MCP servers, not virtual connectors.

Step 5. Now check the actual result. In an approved disposable agent, test the relevant design/publish path and published runtime tool path with an allowed control.

Step 6. Finally, record the claim carefully. Record an actual policy-attributable violation. Do not turn a maker-only error or an agent risk score into universal runtime coverage.

Where to check / when. Here is where to check. Policy environment and connector classification. Exact design/runtime violation and allowed-control outcome. Studio supports real-time violation messages; policy/connection distribution can still have latency. Verify both design-time and the intended runtime path. These illustrative screens do not establish a pass.

Recap. Let's recap. Resolve connector and connection identity. Inspect environment scope/classification. Check the exact endpoint/tool rule. Test design and published runtime separately. Path blocking is not payload inspection. Blocking locally uploaded document knowledge does not block SharePoint/OneDrive knowledge. Keep real evidence in the protected Word validation draft linked on the card.

Can a Studio data policy stop a tool or MCP connector path?Studio data policies govern supported connectors, HTTP, knowledge and channels. Blocking a Power Platform connector also blocks MCP tools relying on that connector. This is a path restriction, not proof of payload inspection.

Who can do this

Least-privileged starting point: Environment Admin for policies within their permitted environment scope. A Power Platform/tenant administrator can manage broader tenant policy scope. A maker can validate their authorized agent path without being granted tenant administration.

How to set it up

  1. Open Power Platform admin center → Security → Data and privacy → Data policy.
  2. Inspect the policy's environment scope and the underlying connector's Business, Non-business or Blocked classification.
  3. Identify the exact tool/MCP server and connection identity. Direct custom MCP paths need separate assessment.
  4. Check the applicable connector/action/endpoint restriction. Advanced connector policies govern supported real connectors/MCP servers, not virtual connectors.
  5. In an approved disposable agent, test the relevant design/publish path and published runtime tool path with an allowed control.
  6. Record an actual policy-attributable violation. Do not turn a maker-only error or an agent risk score into universal runtime coverage.

How long to wait

Studio supports real-time violation messages; policy/connection distribution can still have latency. Verify both design-time and the intended runtime path.

Where to check the result

  • Policy environment and connector classification.
  • Exact design/runtime violation and allowed-control outcome.

Licensing for schools

  • Verify Copilot Studio capacity/licensing and environment governance entitlement.
  • Purview licensing does not by itself configure Power Platform data policies or create telemetry for every MCP implementation.
